episodes.title: Meet Sena and Daniel: What AI Can't Do for You
Reading Emotions on a Video Call

brief_data.summary: Sena practices explaining how she thinks about numbers to her friend Aoi, a nurse, who says she understood four words out of twenty-one. Laura has asked for an informal explanation with no slides at Monday's lunch. Daniel shares Pamela Hinds's curse-of-expertise LEGO study: people who had built the toy five times guessed first-timers would need about 8.5 minutes, while real first-timers needed about 12.5, and a list of tips barely changed their guesses. He tells the story of Leona, a finance partner who nodded through forty minutes of his attrition model and then cut his hiring request in half. In the Japan-vs-US centerpiece, Sena replays a Tokyo report meeting where the number arrives after seven minutes of keii (background) and a Seattle call where Laura says "What's the number, and what do you need from us?" Today's challenge: explain one thing you do to someone outside your field in three sentences, then ask what part didn't land. It ends with Kato-san's message at 7:51 a.m.: Laura has one question for Sena on the eight o'clock call, no prep.
brief_data.hook:
The more you know, the worse you are at guessing what it's like not to know. People who built a LEGO toy five times guessed beginners needed 8.5 minutes. They needed 12.5.
Learn a three-sentence way to explain your work to anyone, no slides.

thumb_notes: Say what it means for them
